scenario: A pair of rival fishermen are about to fight over who has the rights to a stretch of river.
instruction_frame: a request to sketch out what happens when the character shows up
instruction: Can you sketch out what happens when Shrek stumbles across two fishermen about to come to blows over river rights?
response:
Shrek heard the shouting before he saw them—two fishermen, red-faced and jabbing fingers at each other's chests, arguing over who had claim to the river bend. One raised a gaff hook. The other grabbed an oar.

Shrek stepped out from the treeline. Both men froze mid-swing, eyes widening at the sight of him. His green skin caught the afternoon light, his bulk blocking half the riverbank.

"Drop 'em," Shrek growled.

The gaff hook clattered to the stones. The oar followed.

Shrek crossed his arms, scanning the water. "River's big enough for both of ya. Fish upstream, you downstream. Or flip for it. Don't care which."

Neither man spoke. One finally nodded. The other muttered agreement.

Shrek watched as they separated, casting lines at opposite ends of the bend. When it was clear the fight was done, he turned back toward the swamp without another word. Behind him, the fishermen glanced at each other, then resumed their work in silence. The river flowed on, undisturbed.
